questions.q: What record does a Service Catalog trigger in Flow Designer actually fire on?
options: The Request (sc_request) record covering everything in the requester's checkout
The Requested Item (sc_req_item) record, scoped to a specific catalog item
The catalog item definition record itself
A Business Rule attached to the catalog item
questions.explain: The trigger fires on Requested Item Created, filtered by the cat_item field to one specific catalog item.

questions.q: Why does the trigger condition filter on the Requested Item's cat_item field rather than triggering on every Requested Item?
options: Because cat_item doesn't actually exist on the Requested Item table
So the flow only runs for requests of the one catalog item it was built to fulfill, not every item in the catalog
Because filtering is required by ServiceNow licensing
So the flow runs once per Request instead of once per item
questions.explain: Without that filter, any catalog request on any item would fire the same flow execution.

questions.q: A requester checks out with a laptop and a monitor in the same cart. Why does each item get its own flow execution rather than one shared execution?
options: Because the trigger fires on the Requested Item, and each item in a cart gets its own Requested Item record with its own variables
ServiceNow does not allow more than one item per cart
Because the Request record splits itself into two separate requests automatically
Because flows cannot read variables at all, only Requests can
questions.explain: One Request can contain multiple Requested Items; triggering per Requested Item keeps each item's fulfillment logic and variables isolated.

questions.q: Once a catalog-triggered flow starts running, how does it access what the requester actually selected in the catalog item's variables?
options: It cannot access variable values at all — those stay locked to the catalog item form
A developer must hand-code a script to pull variable values from the database
The Requested Item record exposes the variable values as data pills the flow can reference directly
Variable values are only visible in reports, never in a flow
questions.explain: The triggering Requested Item record carries the variable values, available as data pills just like any other trigger output.

questions.q: What replaced the legacy Workflow editor as the place where catalog item fulfillment logic is built in a modern implementation?
options: Fulfillment logic moved into a flow, connected to the catalog item through a Service Catalog trigger
Catalog items no longer support any kind of fulfillment automation
Fulfillment logic now lives directly on the catalog item's form layout
ACLs replaced Workflow for all catalog fulfillment
questions.explain: Flow Designer's trigger-based approach replaces the older default of attaching a Workflow directly to the catalog item.
